subject: AegisPay: Partial Degradation during 2027-01-08 auth maintenance - credit request
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aegispay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 14:32:00 -0000
Subject: Partial degradation observed 09:20-09:55 UTC — request for SLA credit

Hi Vanessa,

We saw a sustained increase in 5xx errors and tail latency for our payment auth flow between ~09:20 and ~09:55 UTC on Jan 8 (attached is our client telemetry aggregated across 4 regions). Impact: ~18% of auth requests failed for our east-us customers which caused failover logic and retries in our checkout flow.

AegisPay relies on Redwood for consistent availability; given the duration and customer impact we're requesting the SLA credit calculation and an explanation of whether this is counted as a Redwood outage, a third-party maintenance overlap, or partial degradation that should be excluded.

Can you confirm timeline (edge ingress → auth proxy → model serving) and share any logs/traces you have? We need this for our internal RCA and for the procurement team who will review on Monday.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Site Reliability Lead, AegisPay

Quick asks so we can correlate our probe data with yours: can you confirm the client IP ranges affected (if available) and whether retries were client-side or triggered by your load balancer? We'll pull edge probe traces + per-region egress logs.

We'll prioritize this and aim to get a preliminary timeline back within 24 hours. If this is urgent for procurement, I'll also prepare a proposed credit allocation so you can review internally.

—Vanessa

Subject: RE: Partial degradation observed 09:20-09:55 UTC — request for SLA credit (prelim findings)

Vanessa / team / Sarah — preliminary findings from infra: we've correlated Redwood edge probes and internal traces with AegisPay's window. Key points: 

- At 09:15 UTC our downstream auth provider (AuthX) had a scheduled maintenance that began at 09:12 UTC and ended at 09:40 UTC. Their bulletin shows a partial service degradation for a subset of regions.
- Our routing layer attempted failover to AuthX's secondary endpoint at ~09:20 UTC but a stale DNS TTL caused some edge nodes (primarily east-us-1) to continue hitting the degraded endpoint until our aggressive cache flush at 09:37 UTC.
- Effect on Redwood: increased error rates and latency for requests that required upstream auth validation; the issue was regionally constrained (east-us) rather than global.

Attachments included: auth-probe-traces.tar.gz (edge traces, per-region probe logs).

Initial thought on SLA: because the root cause includes a third-party scheduled maintenance (AuthX) AND a Redwood routing cache not expiring quickly enough, this is a mixed-responsibility event. We should not automatically classify the whole 09:12–09:40 window as a Redwood exclusion — our DNS TTL handling and failover execution contributed materially from ~09:20–09:37.

I'll prepare a proposed apportionment and a CSV with the minute-by-minute availability tally.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: auth-probe-traces.tar.gz (tar.gz, 4.8MB)
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aegispay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 10:47:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Partial degradation observed 09:20-09:55 UTC — request for SLA credit

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the rapid look. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our telemetry shows the client-facing errors persist until ~09:55 UTC; retries/backoff meant some requests were eventually successful after repeated attempts (which is why our aggregated window looks longer).
- The affected traffic was overwhelmingly from east-us customers; we can confirm retries were mostly client-side (browser SDK) and our load balancer didn't show upstream 5xx at our origin.
- From a contractual perspective, procurement will want an explicit apportionment model. Given the customer impact and observable duration (09:20–09:55 perceived by our users), AegisPay is requesting a 10% credit against Jan monthly usage unless Redwood proposes an equivalent remediation + credit breakdown.

Can you provide a minute-level availability CSV and the logic you'll use to count minutes as "degraded" vs "excluded"? Also please include whether Redwood's fallback DNS behavior is considered an operational misconfiguration for the purposes of SLA adjudication.

Best,
Sarah
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@aegispay.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Partial degradation observed 09:20-09:55 UTC — request for SLA credit (proposal)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and for the clear ask. We've completed the minute-by-minute tallies and a short incident summary (draft attached) and propose the following: 

1) Time windows: 
   - AuthX scheduled maintenance window (AuthX bulletin): 09:12–09:40 UTC (excluded per standard third-party maintenance policy).
   - Redwood residual impact due to DNS cache TTL + failover delay: 09:20–09:37 UTC (17 minutes) — Redwood accepts responsibility for this interval because our edge routing failed to pivot cleanly.
   - Your client-perceived window (09:37–09:55) appears to reflect retries and client-side backoff; we've included these minutes in the detailed CSV but do not attribute those to active Redwood service unavailability once our routing was corrected.

2) Proposed credit:
   - We propose a 5% credit on Jan usage equivalent to the 17-minute Redwood-responsible window (apportioned by your regional traffic share). Attachment slacalc_proposal_20270110.csv contains the minute-level math and region weighting.

3) Remediation & next steps: 
   - We will patch the DNS TTL refresh logic so aggressive cache flushes happen within 60s of downstream health signals.
   - We'll run a joint tabletop with AuthX and AegisPay to validate failover paths (proposed: Jan 18).

If you accept the 5% credit proposal we'll issue the billing credit and finalize the incident report for your procurement team. If you'd like to escalate to Marissa (my manager) for further negotiation we can do that as well.

Link to draft incident doc & calculations: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AegisIncidentDraft

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
